content.title: HR Security Tip: Spotting Fake Job Applicant Attachments
content.summary: Learn how to spot malicious attachments and fraudulent links in candidate applications to keep Nebulon secure.
content.body_markdown:
We all get tricked sometimes, but opening unexpected applicant attachments can expose our network to malware [S6].

Watch out for these 3 red flags:
1. Password-protected archives or unusual file types disguised as resumes [S5, S6].
2. High-urgency wording pushing quick reviews without normal screening [S2].
3. Links asking you to download candidate files or code assessments from unverified sites [S1, S8].

Action:
Always verify suspicious applicant details through official recruitment channels before opening attachments or clicking external links [S2, S8].

If you receive a suspicious job application, forward it to security@nebulon.example.com [ORG].
key_points: Attackers send malicious attachments disguised as job applicant resumes or assessments.
Password-protected archives and external links are commonly used to bypass security filters.
Always verify candidate details independently before opening attachments.
red_flags: Password-protected zip files or executable attachments disguised as applicant resumes.
Urgent or pushy wording demanding quick review or hiring without standard screening.
Links directing you to download resumes or technical assessments from unverified external sites.
actions: Verify candidate details via official recruitment portals before opening attached files or clicking links.
content.report_how: Forward any suspicious applicant emails or attachments to security@nebulon.example.com.

past_modules.summary: Test your ability to spot payment redirect fraud, fake invoices, and unauthorized banking changes with this 5-question Finance quiz.
key_points: Always verify banking detail changes out-of-band using trusted phone numbers [ORG].
Scammers use slight variations in email addresses to spoof trusted contacts [S1].
Unusual urgency and unexpected invoice modifications are major warning signs of billing fraud [S1, S3].
Report suspicious payment requests immediately to security@nebulon.example.com [ORG].

past_modules.summary: Learn how scammers use QR codes in emails to bypass security filters and how you can spot and report quishing attempts safely.
key_points: Criminals send millions of quishing emails daily to hide malicious URLs inside QR-code images [S6].
